title: حِكَايَةُ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ
part: Night 90 · King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 491–494 (Night 90, continuing directly from nights-89), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm as Macnaghten prints it, except where a clear misprint has been corrected (each is noted). Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition’s Middle Arabic forms, is preserved; clear misprints are corrected in the text, and the note on each gives the print’s reading. Obscure or doubtful forms are kept as printed, vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 90 continues the tale of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān. King Afrīdūn perfumes his patriarchs with the “Greatest Incense” and sends out his champion Lūqā, “the Sword of the Messiah”; Sharrukān rides out to meet him, catches the spear Lūqā hurls and kills him with it, and dawn cuts Shahrazād off as the Christians cry out for help. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الْمُوفِيَةُ لِلتِّسْعِينَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-mūfiyatu li-al-tisʿīna
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the completing-one for the ninety,
sentences.i: And when it was the ninetieth night,
sentences.n: The night is numbered “the one that completes the ninety”, the ninetieth.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُ أَنَّهُ لَمَّا أَصْبَحَ الصَّبَاحُ وَأَشْرَقَ بِنُورِهِ وَلَاحَ وَتَبَادَرَتِ الْفُرْسَانُ إِلَى حَمْلِ الرِّمَاحِ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu annahu lammā aṣbaḥa al-ṣabāḥu wa-ashraqa bi-nūrihi wa-lāḥa wa-tabādarati al-fursānu ilā ḥamli al-rimāḥi
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king the happy, that when the morning dawned, and shone with its light, and appeared, and the horsemen hastened to the bearing of the lances,
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that when morning dawned, shone with its light and spread, and the horsemen hurried to take up their lances,

sentences.t: دَعَا الْمَلِكُ أَفْرِيدُونُ بِخَوَاصِّ بَطَارِقَتِهِ وَأَرْبَابِ دَوْلَتِهِ وَخَلَعَ عَلَيْهِمْ وَنَقَشَ الصَّلِيبَ فِي وُجُوهِهِمْ وَبَخَّرَهُمْ بِالْبَخُورِ الْمُتَقَدِّمِ ذِكْرُهُ الَّذِي هُوَ خُرْوُ الْبَطْرِيقِ الْأَكْبَرِ وَالْكَاهِنِ الْأَذْكَرِ
sentences.tr: daʿā al-maliku afrīdūnu bi-khawāṣṣi baṭāriqatihi wa-arbābi dawlatihi wa-khalaʿa ʿalayhim wa-naqasha al-ṣalība fī wujūhihim wa-bakhkharahum bi-al-bakhūri al-mutaqaddimi dhikruhu alladhī huwa khurʾu al-baṭrīqi al-akbari wa-al-kāhini al-adhkari
sentences.l: the king Afrīdūn called for the chosen-ones of his patriarchs and the lords of his state, and bestowed robes on them, and engraved the cross on their faces, and perfumed them with the incense, the before-going its mention, which is the dung of the patriarch the greatest and the priest the most-mentioned,
sentences.i: King Afrīdūn summoned the chief of his patriarchs and the lords of his realm, gave them robes of honour, marked the cross on their faces, and perfumed them with the incense mentioned before, which is the dung of the Greatest Patriarch and the Most Renowned Priest,
sentences.n: The “incense” is the patriarch’s excrement, as in the last night. خرو is a Middle Arabic spelling (the classical word is خَرْء); it is vocalised accordingly.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا بَخَّرَهُمْ دَعَا بِحُضُورِهِ لُوقَا ابْنَ شَمْلُوطَ الَّذِي يُسَمُّونَهُ سَيْفَ الْمَسِيحِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā bakhkharahum daʿā bi-ḥuḍūrihi lūqā ibna shamlūṭa alladhī yusammūnahu sayfa al-masīḥi
sentences.l: And when he had perfumed them, he called to his presence Lūqā son of Shamlūṭ, whom they name the Sword of the Messiah,
sentences.i: When he had perfumed them, he called before him Lūqā son of Shamlūṭ, whom they call the Sword of the Messiah,
sentences.n: The name is printed شملوط here and شلموط (Shalmūṭ) near the end of the night; both are kept as printed. دعا بـ means “call for, send for”.

sentences.t: وَبَخَّرَهُ بِالرَّجِيعِ وَحَكَّهُ بِهِ بَعْدَ التَّبْخِيرِ وَنَشَّقَهُ وَلَطَّخَ لَهُ عَوَارِضَهُ وَمَسَحَ بِالنَّخْلَةِ شَوَارِبَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-bakhkharahu bi-al-rajīʿi wa-ḥakkahu bihi baʿda al-tabkhīri wa-nashshaqahu wa-laṭṭakha lahu ʿawāriḍahu wa-masaḥa bi-al-nakhlati shawāribahu
sentences.l: and he perfumed him with the droppings, and rubbed him with it after the perfuming, and made him snuff it up, and smeared for him his cheeks, and wiped with the palm-frond his moustaches.
sentences.i: He perfumed him with the dung, rubbed him with it after the fumigation, made him sniff it, smeared his cheeks, and wiped his moustaches with a palm-frond.
sentences.n: The print is frank and mocking about the Christians’ rite; it is translated as printed. The detail of the palm-frond (النخلة) is obscure; it is read as the thing the dung was wiped on with.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ ذَلِكَ الْمَلْعُونُ لُوقَا مَا فِي بِلَادِ الرُّومِ أَعْظَمُ مِنْهُ وَلَا أَرْمَى بِالنِّبَالِ وَلَا أَضْرَبُ بِالسَّيْفِ وَلَا أَطْعَنُ مِنْهُ بِالرُّمْحِ يَوْمَ النِّزَالِ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna dhālika al-malʿūnu lūqā mā fī bilādi al-rūmi aʿẓamu minhu wa-lā armā bi-al-nibāli wa-lā aḍrabu bi-al-sayfi wa-lā aṭʿanu minhu bi-al-rumḥi yawma al-nizāli
sentences.l: And that accursed one, Lūqā — there was not in the lands of Rūm one greater than he, nor more casting with arrows, nor more striking with the sword, nor more thrusting than he with the lance on the day of combat.
sentences.i: That accursed Lūqā had no equal in the lands of Rūm: none greater than he, none better with the arrow, none keener with the sword, none fiercer with the lance on the day of combat.
sentences.n: “Rūm” is the Byzantine and Christian lands in general. The comparatives (أرمى، أضرب، أطعن) are “more casting, more striking, more thrusting”.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ بَشِعَ الْمَنْظَرِ كَأَنَّ وَجْهَهُ وَجْهُ حِمَارٍ وَصُورَتَهُ صُورَةُ قِرْدٍ وَطَلْعَتَهُ طَلْعَةُ الرَّقِيبِ وَقُرْبَهُ أَصْعَبُ مِنْ فِرَاقِ الْحَبِيبِ لَهُ مِنَ اللَّيْلِ ظُلْمَتُهُ وَمِنَ الْأَسَدِ نَكْهَتُهُ وَمِنَ النَّمِرِ وَقَاحَتُهُ وَمِنَ الْكُفْرِ سِيمَتُهُ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna bashiʿa al-manẓari ka-anna wajhahu wajhu ḥimārin wa-ṣūratahu ṣūratu qirdin wa-ṭalʿatahu ṭalʿatu al-raqībi wa-qurbahu aṣʿabu min firāqi al-ḥabībi lahu mina al-layli ẓulmatuhu wa-mina al-asadi nakhhatuhu wa-mina al-namiri waqāḥatuhu wa-mina al-kufri sīmatuhu
sentences.l: And he was ugly of sight, as if his face were the face of an ass, and his form the form of an ape, and his countenance the countenance of the spy; and his nearness was harder than the parting from the beloved. He had of the night its darkness, and of the lion its breath, and of the leopard its impudence, and of unbelief its mark.
sentences.i: He was hideous to look at: his face the face of an ass, his shape the shape of an ape, his looks those of a jealous watcher, and being near him harder to bear than parting from a loved one. He had the darkness of night, the breath of a lion, the insolence of a leopard and the stamp of unbelief.
sentences.n: Rhymed, balanced prose (sajʿ). The print has وجههه with a third ه; it is a misprint for وجهه “his face”, corrected here. الرقيب is the watcher or rival who spoils lovers’ meetings, a stock figure of love poetry.

sentences.t: وَبَعْدَ ذَلِكَ أَقْبَلَ عَلَى الْمَلِكِ أَفْرِيدُونَ وَقَبَّلَ قَدَمَيْهِ ثُمَّ وَقَفَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ فَقَالَ لَهُ الْمَلِكُ أَفْرِيدُونُ إِنِّي أُرِيدُأَنْ تَبْرُزَ إِلَى شَرْكَانَ مَلِكِ دِمَشْقَ ابْنِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ وَقَدِ انْجَلَى عَنَّا هَذَا الشَّرُّوَهُمَانُ
sentences.tr: wa-baʿda dhālika aqbala ʿalā al-maliki afrīdūna wa-qabbala qadamayhi thumma waqafa bayna yadayhi fa-qāla lahu al-maliku afrīdūnu innī urīdu an tabruza ilā sharrukāna maliki dimashqa ibni ʿumara ibni al-nuʿmāni wa-qadi injalā ʿannā hādhā al-sharru wa-humān
sentences.l: And after that he came forward to the king Afrīdūn and kissed his feet, then stood between his hands. And the king Afrīdūn said to him: I want you to go out to Sharrukān, king of Damascus, son of ʿUmar son of al-Nuʿmān, and there has cleared from us this evil, and Humān.
sentences.i: After that he came before King Afrīdūn, kissed his feet and stood in front of him. The king said to him, “I want you to go out against Sharrukān, king of Damascus, son of ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, now that this trouble has cleared away from us.”
sentences.n: The print’s هذا الشروهمان is doubtful and is kept as printed: read as هَذَا الشَّرُّ وَهُمَانُ, “this evil” followed by a word, وهمان, that cannot be identified; the sense, that the danger has passed, is clear from the context, so the idiomatic version leaves it out. اريدان is printed run together; read as أُرِيدُ أَنْ.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ سَمْعًا وَطَاعَةً ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْمَلِكَ نَقَشَ فِي وَجْهِهِ الصَّلِيبَ وَزَعَمَ أَنَّ النَّصْرَ يَحْصُلُ لَهُ عَنْ قَرِيبٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla samʿan wa-ṭāʿatan thumma inna al-malika naqasha fī wajhihi al-ṣalība wa-zaʿama anna al-naṣra yaḥṣulu lahu ʿan qarībin
sentences.l: And he said: Hearing and obedience. Then the king engraved the cross on his face and claimed that victory would come to him from nearness.
sentences.i: He answered, “With hearing and obedience.” Then the king marked the cross on his face and declared that victory would soon be his.
sentences.n: عن قريب is “before long, soon” (literally “from near”).

sentences.t: ثُمَّ انْصَرَفَ لُوقَا مِنْ عِنْدِ الْمَلِكِ أَفْرِيدُونَ وَرَكِبَ الْمَلْعُونُ لُوقَا جَوَادًا أَشْقَرَ وَعَلَيْهِ ثَوْبٌ أَحْمَرُ وَزَرَدِيَّةٌ مِنَ الذَّهَبِ الْمُرَصَّعِ بِالْجَوْهَرِ وَحَمَلَ رِجَالُهُ ثُلْثَ حِرَابٍ كَأَنَّهُ إِبْلِيسُ اللَّعِينُ يَوْمَ الْأَحْزَابِ وَتَوَجَّهَ هُوَ وَحِزْبُهُ الْكُفَّارُ كَأَنَّهُمْ يُسَاقُونَ إِلَى النَّارِ
sentences.tr: thumma inṣarafa lūqā min ʿindi al-maliki afrīdūna wa-rakiba al-malʿūnu lūqā jawādan ashqara wa-ʿalayhi thawbun aḥmaru wa-zaradiyyatun mina al-dhahabi al-muraṣṣaʿi bi-al-jawhari wa-ḥamala rijāluhu thulta ḥirābin ka-annahu iblīsu al-laʿīnu yawma al-aḥzābi wa-tawajjaha huwa wa-ḥizbuhu al-kuffāru ka-annahum yusāqūna ilā al-nāri
sentences.l: Then Lūqā went away from the presence of the king Afrīdūn, and the accursed Lūqā rode a chestnut steed, and on him a red robe and a coat of mail of gold set with jewels, and his men carried three lances, as if he were Iblīs the accursed on the day of the Confederates, and he set out, he and his party of unbelievers, as if they were being driven to the Fire.
sentences.i: Lūqā left King Afrīdūn’s presence, and the accursed Lūqā mounted a chestnut horse, wearing a red robe and a mail-coat of gold set with jewels, while his men bore three lances, so that he seemed Iblīs himself on the Day of the Confederates. He set out with his party of unbelievers, as though they were being driven to the Fire.
sentences.n: ثلث is the print’s spelling of ثلاث “three” (the edition omits the long alif); it is kept. يوم الأحزاب is the day of the siege of Medina by the Confederates, a Qurʾānic reference.

sentences.t: وَبَيْنَهُمْ مُنَادٍيُنَادِي بِالْعَرَبِيِّ وَيَقُولُ يَا أُمَّةَ مُحَمَّدٍ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ لَا يَخْرُجُ مِنْكُمْ إِلَّا فَارِسُكُمْ سَيْفُ الْإِسْلَامِ شَرْكَانُ صَاحِبُ دِمَشْقَ الشَّامِ
sentences.tr: wa-baynahum munādin yunādī bi-al-ʿarabiyyi wa-yaqūlu yā ummata muḥammadin ṣallā allāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallama lā yakhruju minkum illā fārisukum sayfu al-islāmi sharrukānu ṣāḥibu dimashqa al-shāmi
sentences.l: And among them a crier crying in the Arabic, and saying: O community of Muḥammad, God bless him and give him peace, let none come out from among you except your horseman, the Sword of Islam, Sharrukān, lord of Damascus of Syria.
sentences.i: Among them a herald cried out in Arabic: “People of Muḥammad, God bless him and give him peace, let none come out from among you but your own horseman, the Sword of Islam, Sharrukān, lord of Damascus in Syria!”
sentences.n: The print runs منادينادي together; it is read as منادٍ ينادي “a crier crying”, and the spacing is kept as printed. The Arabic of the sentence is marked as the Christians’ foreign tongue, whence بالعربي “in Arabic”.

sentences.t: فَمَا اسْتَتَمَّ كَلَامَهُ إِلَّا وَضَجَّةٌ فِى الْفَلَا سَمِعَ صَوْتَهَا جَمِيعُ الْمَلَا وَرَكَضَاتٌ فَرَّقَتِ الصَّفَّيْنِ وَأَذْكَرَتْ يَوْمَ حُنَيْنٍ فَفَزِعَ اللِّئَامُ مِنْهَا وَأَلْفَتُوا الْأَعْنَاقَ نَحْوَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-mā istatamma kalāmahu illā wa-ḍajjatun fī al-falā samiʿa ṣawtahā jamīʿu al-malā wa-rakaḍātun farraqati al-ṣaffayni wa-adhkarat yawma ḥunaynin fa-fazaʿa al-li-ʾāmu minhā wa-alfatū al-aʿnāqa naḥwahā
sentences.l: He had not finished his speech but a clamour in the wilderness, whose sound all the assembly heard, and gallopings that parted the two ranks and recalled the day of Ḥunayn, and the base-ones were frightened by it and turned the necks toward it.
sentences.i: He had barely finished speaking when a clamour rose on the plain, heard by the whole host, and a thunder of hooves split the two lines and recalled the day of Ḥunayn. The villains were terrified by it and turned their necks towards it.
sentences.n: The print has والفتوا, read as وَأَلْفَتُوا “and they turned”; it is probably a slip for والتفتوا (with the ت dropped), but more than one reading is possible, so it is kept as printed and vocalised by the sense. The day of Ḥunayn was a famous battle of the Prophet’s time, in which the Muslim ranks were first shaken and then rallied.

sentences.t: وَإِذَا هُوَ الْمَلِكُ شَرْكَانُ ابْنُ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ وَكَانَ أَخُوهُ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ لَمَّا رَأَى ذَلِكَ الْمَلْعُونَ فِى الْمَيْدَانِ وَسَمِعَ الْمُنَادِيَ الْتَفَتَ لِأَخِيهِ شَرْكَانَ وَقَالَ لَهُ إِنَّهُمْ يُرِيدُونَكَ
sentences.tr: wa-idhā huwa al-maliku sharrukānu ibnu al-maliki ʿumara ibni al-nuʿmāni wa-kāna akhūhu ḍawʾu al-makāni lammā raʾā dhālika al-malʿūna fī al-maydāni wa-samiʿa al-munādiya iltafata li-akhīhi sharrukāna wa-qāla lahu innahum yurīdūnaka
sentences.l: And behold, it was the king Sharrukān, son of the king ʿUmar son of al-Nuʿmān; and his brother Ḍawʾ al-Makān, when he saw that accursed one in the field and heard the crier, turned to his brother Sharrukān and said to him: They want you.
sentences.i: And there was King Sharrukān, son of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān. His brother Ḍawʾ al-Makān, when he saw that accursed man in the field and heard the herald, turned to Sharrukān and said, “It is you they want.”
sentences.n: The print has اخوة, a misprint for اخوه, corrected here. (The edition regularly spells “his brother” with ه for ة; the printed ة is the slip.)

sentences.t: فَقَالَ إِنْ كَانَ الْأَمْرُ كَذَلِكَ فَهُوَ أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla in kāna al-amru ka-dhālika fa-huwa aḥabbu ilayya
sentences.l: And he said: If the matter is thus, then it is dearer to me.
sentences.i: He said, “If that is how it is, I like it all the better.”

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا تَحَقَّقُوا الْأَمْرَ وَسَمِعُوا هَذَا الْمُنَادِيَ وَهُوَ يَقُولُ فِى الْمَيْدَانِ لَا يَبْرُزْلِي إِلَّا شَرْكَانُ عَلِمُوا أَنَّ هَذَا الْمَلْعُونَ فَارِسُ بِلَادِ الرُّومِ وَكَانَ قَدْ حَلَفَ أَنْ يُخَلِّىَ الْأَرْضَ مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ وَإِلَّا فَهُوَ مِنْ أَخْسَرِ الْخَاسِرِينَ لِأَنَّهُ هُوَ الَّذِي حَرَّقَ الْأَكْبَادَ وَفَزِعَتْ مِنْ شَرِّهِ الْأَجْنَادُ مِنَ التُّرْكِ وَالدَّيْلَمِ وَالْأَكْرَادِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā taḥaqqaqū al-amra wa-samiʿū hādhā al-munādiya wa-huwa yaqūlu fī al-maydāni lā yabruz lī illā sharrukānu ʿalimū anna hādhā al-malʿūna fārisu bilādi al-rūmi wa-kāna qad ḥalafa an yukhalliya al-arḍa mina al-muslimīna wa-illā fa-huwa min akhsari al-khāsirīna li-annahu huwa alladhī ḥarraqa al-akbāda wa-fazaʿat min sharrihi al-ajnādu mina al-turki wa-al-daylami wa-al-akrādi
sentences.l: And when they were sure of the matter and heard this crier saying in the field, “Let none go out to me but Sharrukān,” they knew that this accursed one was the horseman of the lands of Rūm, and he had sworn to empty the earth of the Muslims, or else he would be among the greatest of the losers, because he it was who had burned the livers, and the armies were frightened by his evil, of the Turks and the Daylamites and the Kurds.
sentences.i: When they were sure of what was happening and heard the herald calling in the field, “Let none come out to me but Sharrukān,” they knew that this accursed man was the champion of the lands of Rūm. He had sworn to rid the earth of the Muslims or be counted among the greatest of the losers, for it was he who had set hearts burning and filled the armies with fear of his evil — Turks, Daylamites and Kurds alike.
sentences.n: لا يبرزلي is printed run together; it is read as لا يَبْرُزْ لِي “let none go out to me”, with the jussive of the negative command. “Burned the livers” means “caused grief”: the liver is the seat of feeling. The Daylam are the people of the Caspian highlands.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ بَرَزَإِلَيْهِ شَرْكَانُ كَأَنَّهُ أَسَدٌ غَضْبَانُ وَكَانَ رَاكِبًا عَلَى ظَهْرِ جَوَادٍ يُشْبِهُ شَارِدَ الْغِزْلَانِ فَسَاقَهُ نَحْوَ لُوقَا حَتَّى صَارَ عِنْدَهُ وَهَزَّ الرُّمْحَ فِي يَدِهِ كَأَنَّهُ أَفْعَى مِنَ الْحَيَّاتِ وَأَنْشَدَ هَذِهِ الْأَبْ—يَاتَ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika baraza ilayhi sharrukānu ka-annahu asadun ghaḍbānu wa-kāna rākiban ʿalā ẓahri jawādin yushbihu shārida al-ghizlāni fa-sāqahu naḥwa lūqā ḥattā ṣāra ʿindahu wa-hazza al-rumḥa fī yadihi ka-annahu afʿā mina al-ḥayyāti wa-anshada hādhihi al-abyāta
sentences.l: And at that Sharrukān went out to him, as if he were an angry lion, and he was riding on the back of a steed resembling the fleeing of gazelles, and he drove it toward Lūqā until he was beside him, and shook the lance in his hand as if it were a viper of the snakes, and he recited these verses.
sentences.i: Then Sharrukān rode out to meet him like an angry lion, on a steed like a bolting gazelle. He drove it towards Lūqā until he was beside him, brandished the lance in his hand like a viper among snakes, and recited these verses:
sentences.n: The print breaks الأبيات with a dash at the line end; the dash is kept. شارد الغزلان means gazelles that have bolted; it is read as a simile for the horse’s speed.

sentences.t:
لِيْ اَشْقَرُ سَمْحُ الْعِنَانِ مُغَائِرُ * يُعْطِيكَ مَا يُرْضِيكَ مِنْ مَجْهُودِهِ
وَمُثَقَّفٌ لَدْنُ السِّنَانِ كَاَنَّمَا * اُمُّ الْمَنَايَا رُكِّبَتْ فِيْ عُودِهِ
وَمُهَنَّدٌ عَضْبٌ اِذَا جَرَّدْتَهُ * خِلْتَ الْبُرُوقَ تَمُوجُ فِيْ تَجْرِيدِهِ
sentences.tr:
lī ashqaru samḥu al-ʿināni mughāʾiru * yuʿṭīka mā yurḍīka min majhūdihi
wa-muthaqqafun laduna al-sinān ka-annamā * ummu al-manāyā rukkibat fī ʿūdihi
wa-muhannadun ʿaḍbun idhā jarradtahu * khilta al-burūqa tamūju fī tajrīdihi
sentences.l:
I have a chestnut, easy of rein, fiercely-jealous, * he gives you what pleases you of his utmost effort,
and a straightened one, supple of point, as if * the mother of deaths were set in its shaft,
and a sword Indian-wrought, cutting, when you draw it * you imagine lightnings surging in its drawing.
sentences.i:
I have a chestnut with easy rein and a fiery spirit; * he gives you of his utmost all that you could want.
I have a straightened lance whose point is supple, as if * the mother of deaths were set in its shaft,
and a keen Indian blade: when you draw it, * you would think lightning surged in its unsheathing.
sentences.n: Verse copied exactly as the edition prints it, marks and all (the print points اَشْقَرُ and كَاَنَّمَا with bare alif and fatḥa, as it does throughout). The three lines name Sharrukān’s three weapons: his chestnut horse, his lance and his sword. “Mother of deaths” (ummu al-manāyā) is a poetic figure for the lance’s deadly head. The hemistichs are not further rendered word for word where the sense is figurative.

sentences.t: فَلَمْ يَفْهَمْ لُوقَا مَعْنَى هَذَا الْكَلَامِ وَلَاحَمَاسَ هَذَا النِّظَامِ بَلْ لَطَمَ وَجْهَهُ بِيَدِهِ تَعْظِيمًا لِلصَّلِيبِ الْمَنْقُوشِ عَلَيْهِ ثُمَّ قَبَّلَهَا وَأَشْرَعَ الرُّمْحَ نَحْوَ شَرْكَانَ
sentences.tr: fa-lam yafham lūqā maʿnā hādhā al-kalāmi wa-lā ḥamāsa hādhā al-niẓāmi bal laṭama wajhahu bi-yadihi taʿẓīman li-al-ṣalībi al-manqūshi ʿalayhi thumma qabbalahā wa-ashraʿa al-rumḥa naḥwa sharrukāna
sentences.l: But Lūqā did not understand the meaning of this speech, nor the fervour of this arrangement, but struck his face with his hand in veneration of the cross engraved on it, then kissed it, and levelled the lance toward Sharrukān.
sentences.i: Lūqā understood neither the meaning of these words nor the fire of the verse. He struck his own face with his hand in reverence for the cross marked on it, kissed the hand, and levelled his lance at Sharrukān.
sentences.n: The print joins ولا حماس as one word; it is kept as printed. حماس is “fervour, zeal”; the word is read as such though it is rare in this sense.

sentences.t: وَكَرَّ عَلَيْهِ ثُمَّ طَوَّحَ الْحَرْبَةَ بِإِحْدَى يَدَيْهِ حَتَّى خَفِيَتْ عَنْ أَعْيُنِ النَّاظِرِينَ وَتَلَقَّاهَا بِالْيَدِ الْأُخْرَى كَفِعْلِ السَّاحِرِينَ
sentences.tr: wa-karra ʿalayhi thumma ṭawwaḥa al-ḥarbata bi-iḥdā yadayhi ḥattā khafiyat ʿan aʿyuni al-nāẓirīna wa-talaqqāhā bi-al-yadi al-ukhrā ka-fiʿli al-sāḥirīna
sentences.l: And he charged at him, then flung the spear with one of his two hands until it was hidden from the eyes of the lookers, and caught it with the other hand, like the doing of the sorcerers.
sentences.i: He charged at him, then tossed the spear up with one hand until it vanished from the sight of the onlookers, and caught it in the other like a conjuror.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ رَمَى بِهَا شَرْكَانَ فَخَرَجَتْ مِنْ يَدِهِ كَأَنَّهَا شِهَابٌ ثَاقِبٌ فَضَجَّتِ النَّاسُ وَخَافُوا عَلَى شَرْكَانَ فَلَمَّا قَرُبَتِ الْحَرْبَةُ مِنْ شَرْكَانَ اخْتَطَفَهَا مِنَ الْهَوَى فَتَحَيَّرَتْ عُقُولُ الْوَرَى
sentences.tr: thumma ramā bihā sharrukāna fa-kharajat min yadihi ka-annahā shihābun thāqibun fa-ḍajjati al-nāsu wa-khāfū ʿalā sharrukāna fa-lammā qarubati al-ḥarbatu min sharrukāna ikhtaṭafahā mina al-hawā fa-taḥayyarat ʿuqūlu al-warā
sentences.l: Then he threw it at Sharrukān, and it went out from his hand as if it were a piercing meteor, and the people clamoured and feared for Sharrukān; and when the spear drew near to Sharrukān, he snatched it from the air, and the minds of mankind were bewildered.
sentences.i: Then he hurled it at Sharrukān, and it left his hand like a piercing meteor. The people cried out in fear for Sharrukān, but when the spear came near him he snatched it out of the air, and everyone was dumbfounded.
sentences.n: The print has ثانب, a misprint for ثاقب, corrected here (شهاب ثاقب, “a piercing meteor”, is Qurʾānic). الهوى here is the Middle Arabic spelling of الهواء “the air”; it is kept as printed. الناس takes a feminine verb (فضجت) as a collective.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ شَرْكَانَ هَزَّهَا بِيَدِهِ الَّتِي أَخَذَهَا بِهَا مِنَ النَّصْرَانِيِّ حَتَّى كَادَأَنْ يَقْصِفَهَا وَرَمَاهَا فِى الْجَوِّ حَتَّى خَفِيَتْ عَنِ النَّظَرِ وَالْتَقَاهَا بِيَدِهِ الثَّانِيَةِ فِي أَقْرَبَ مِنْ لَمْحِ الْبَصَرِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna sharrukāna hazzahā bi-yadihi allatī akhadhahā bihā mina al-naṣrāniyyi ḥattā kāda an yaqṣifahā wa-ramāhā fī al-jawwi ḥattā khafiyat ʿani al-naẓari wa-iltaqāhā bi-yadihi al-thāniyati fī aqraba min lamḥi al-baṣari
sentences.l: Then Sharrukān shook it with his hand with which he had taken it from the Nazarene, until he almost broke it, and cast it into the air until it was hidden from sight, and met it with his second hand in nearer than the glance of the eye.
sentences.i: Then Sharrukān shook it in the hand that had taken it from the Christian until it nearly snapped, and threw it up into the air until it was lost to sight, and caught it in his other hand quicker than the blink of an eye.
sentences.n: The print has لمج, a misprint for لمح (لمح البصر, “the blink of an eye”), corrected here. حتى كاد ان is printed run together (كادان); the spacing is kept. النصراني “the Nazarene” is the usual word for a Christian.

sentences.t: وَصَاحَ صَيْحَةً مِنْ صَمِيمِ قَلْبِهِ وَقَالَ وَحَقِّ مَنْ خَلَقَ السَّبْعَ الطِّبَاقَ لَأَجْعَلَنَّ هَذَا اللَّعِينَ شُهْرَةً فِى الْآفَاقِ
sentences.tr: wa-ṣāḥa ṣayḥatan min ṣamīmi qalbihi wa-qāla wa-ḥaqqi man khalaqa al-sabʿa al-ṭibāqa la-ajʿalanna hādhā al-laʿīna shuhratan fī al-āfāqi
sentences.l: And he cried a cry from the core of his heart, and said: By the right of Him who created the seven strata, I will surely make this accursed one a fame in the horizons.
sentences.i: He let out a shout from the depths of his heart and cried, “By the truth of Him who created the seven heavens, I will make this wretch an example known in every land!”
sentences.n: السبع الطباق is the seven heavens, layered one above another (Qurʾān 67:3). شهرة, “fame, notoriety”, means a spectacle that all will talk of.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ رَمَاهُ بِالْحَرْبَةِ فَأَرَادَ لُوقَا أَنْ يَفْعَلَ بِالْحَرْبَةِ كَمَا فَعَلَ شَرْكَانُ وَمَدَّيَدَهُ إِلَى الْحَرْبَةِ لِيَخْتَطِفَهَا مِنَ الصُّوَى فَعَاجَلَهُ شَرْكَانُ بِضَرْبَةٍ ثَانِيَةٍ وَضَرَبَهُ بِهَا فَوَقَعَتْ فِي وَسَطِ الصَّلِيبِ الَّذِي فِي وَجْهِهِ وَعَجَّلَ اللَّهُ بِرُوحِهِ إِلَى النَّارِ وَبِئْسَ الْقَرَارُ
sentences.tr: thumma ramāhu bi-al-ḥarbati fa-arāda lūqā an yafʿala bi-al-ḥarbati ka-mā faʿala sharrukānu wa-madda yadahu ilā al-ḥarbati li-yakhtaṭifahā mina al-ṣuwā fa-ʿājalahu sharrukānu bi-ḍarbatin thāniyatin wa-ḍarabahu bihā fa-waqaʿat fī wasaṭi al-ṣalībi alladhī fī wajhihi wa-ʿajjala allāhu bi-rūḥihi ilā al-nāri wa-biʾsa al-qarāru
sentences.l: Then he threw the spear at him, and Lūqā wished to do with the spear as Sharrukān had done, and stretched his hand to the spear to snatch it from the waymarks; but Sharrukān forestalled him with a second blow, and struck him with it, and it fell in the middle of the cross that was on his face, and God hastened his soul to the Fire, and wretched is the abode.
sentences.i: Then he hurled the spear at him, and Lūqā tried to do with it what Sharrukān had done and stretched out his hand to snatch it from the air; but Sharrukān forestalled him with a second stroke, striking him with it so that it fell in the middle of the cross on his face, and God hurried his soul to the Fire — an evil resting-place.
sentences.n: The print has الصوى, “the waymarks, the stone signposts of the desert”. It looks like a slip for الهوى “the air” (the same word as in the unit above), but the reading is not certain, so it is kept as printed and the sense “from the air” is given in the idiomatic version. وبئس القرار “and wretched is the abode” echoes the Qurʾān (14:29).

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَى الْكُفَّارُ لُوقَا ابْنَ شَلْمُوطَ وَقَعَ مَقْتُولًا لَطَمُوا عَلَى وُجُوهِهِمْ وَنَادَوْا بِالْوَيْلِ وَالثُّبُورِ وَاسْتَغَاثُوا بِبَطَارِقَةِ الدُّيُورِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾā al-kuffāru lūqā ibna shalmūṭa waqaʿa maqtūlan laṭamū ʿalā wujūhihim wa-nādaw bi-al-waylī wa-al-thubūri wa-istaghāthū bi-baṭāriqati al-duyūri
sentences.l: And when the unbelievers saw Lūqā son of Shalmūṭ fallen slain, they struck their faces and cried out woe and perdition, and called for help on the patriarchs of the monasteries.
sentences.i: When the unbelievers saw Lūqā son of Shalmūṭ fallen dead, they beat their faces, cried out “Woe and ruin!” and called on the patriarchs of the monasteries for help.
sentences.n: The night closes here, mid-battle, as is the way of Shahrazād’s nights. For the name see the earlier note: شلموط here, شملوط above.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُ—بَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka shahra zāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the permitted speech.
sentences.i: Morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted speech.
sentences.n: The closing formula, as in every night; the print splits the name into شهر and زاد and breaks the last word with a dash.
